risks.note: Management names 'intense price competition' among the major risks it has identified. The MD&A adds that while volume growth stayed strong, 'the value growth in the industry has seen a slow-down due to an intense competitive environment fuelled by new entrants as well as some of the legacy players fighting for market share', and that competitive intensity is driving a sharp structural shift towards hard luggage AT VALUE PRICING - i.e. mix is moving toward a category the Company must serve at lower realisations, which is precisely why the premiumisation and in-house premium manufacturing push is being funded.
risks.risk: Intense price competition and value-growth compression in the luggage industry

risks.note: Listed by management as a major identified risk. The MD&A opens by noting several geo-political disruptions globally that directly impacted the global economy and particularly the travel industry, and the Outlook section concedes 'several uncertainties due to larger geo-political factors' even while the Company has grown ahead of the market. Management states future growth prospects and cash flow generation could be materially impacted by these risks.
risks.risk: Cost risk from global geo-political upheaval

risks.note: Explicitly named by management as a major risk. The Company imports inputs and finished backpacks, and continues to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China, so rupee depreciation feeds directly into landed cost in a category where value pricing limits the ability to pass it through.

The Company states it has diversified Backpack supplies by building a larger supplier base within India 'while continuing to retain key vendors based in Bangladesh and China', explicitly to de-risk against potential geo-political and macro-economic uncertainties - the mitigation itself confirms residual cross-border sourcing exposure in a category management calls a strong growth driver. The BRSR material-issues table separately flags Sustainable Supply Chain as a risk with negative financial implications, since gaps at supplier locations may lead to operational disruption, reputational exposure and regulatory concerns.
risks.risk: Supplier and sourcing concentration in the Backpack category (Bangladesh and China)

risks.note: Growth depends on domestic travel and marriage/wedding demand. Geo-political headwinds have already caused a loss of demand for international travel, and the shift towards domestic destinations 'has impacted the size mix away from larger sized luggage to medium sized luggage and cabin size' - smaller units at lower price points. Management's own instruction for the year ahead is to stay focussed on specific channels, categories and consumer segments expected to drive market growth.
risks.risk: Demand is discretionary and travel-linked, with an adverse size-mix shift

risks.note: The BRSR grievance table shows customer complaints filed rose to 1,51,444 in FY 2025-26 from 97,382 in FY 2024-25, with 1,395 pending at year end which the Company says 'will be attended/resolved during FY 2026-27' (the prior year's pending complaints had been resolved). In a brand-led category where consumers are said to prioritise warranties and quality, a step-up of this size is a warranty-cost and brand-equity watch item.

The BRSR material-issues table classifies Climate Strategy & Emission Management as a RISK with negative financial implications: physical impacts such as extreme weather affect operations, logistics and supply chains, while transition factors including regulation and market expectations can affect long-term performance. Against this, the Company's own disclosed trajectory has moved the wrong way - Scope 1 and 2 emissions rose 26% and energy intensity rose 11% versus the FY 2024 baseline, driven by the scaled-up Jaipur plant, against FY 2028 targets of 25% and 20% REDUCTIONS respectively.
risks.risk: Climate transition and physical risk to operations, logistics and supply chains

risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table classifies Occupational Health & Safety as a RISK with negative financial implications: workplace incidents may lead to injuries, disruption and financial exposure, with direct implications for regulatory compliance and continuity of operations. Exposure is structurally elevated because the great majority of the workforce is 'other than permanent' - 2,200 of 2,223 workers and 2,956 of 4,012 employees - across injection-moulding and automated manufacturing operations.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across three manufacturing plants and a largely non-permanent workforce
